> A list of 1,698 gene names is not a finding. Today you turn one into a
> sentence, and then check whether the sentence is real.
>
> Pi writes the code and you decide what it means. Ask it to use the three
> result tables from the setup chunk, and to put its code under the step you are
> working on.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

d <- read_counts("instructional")

# The three result tables you saved in notebook 04. If one is missing, this
# stops and tells you which step of notebook 04 makes it.
read_result <- function(file, where) {
  path <- here("data", file)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop("Could not find ", path, "\nGo back to notebook 04, ", where,
         ", and ask Pi to save the results table there.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

genes_by_outcome   <- read_result("genes_by_outcome.csv",   "Exercise 2, step 5")
genes_by_community <- read_result("genes_by_community.csv", "Exercise 1, step 1")
species_by_outcome <- read_result("species_by_outcome.csv", "Exercise 2, step 3")
```

```{r}
# Each should have one row per feature and a `stat` column.
nrow(genes_by_outcome)
nrow(genes_by_community)
nrow(species_by_outcome)
```

## Part 2 — Ask, look, decide

### Step 1: run the enrichment

Suggested request: *Using `genes_by_outcome` from the setup chunk, make a
ranking vector from `stat`, named by the Ensembl ID in `feature`, with missing
values dropped. Get the human Hallmark sets with msigdbr, using Ensembl IDs.
Run `fgsea(sets, stat, minSize = 15, maxSize = 500)` and sort by `padj`.*

- Genes in the ranking, and how many of them appear in at least one set?
  - *Your answer:*

```{r}
# The ranking: one number per gene, the DESeq2 Wald statistic. Positive stat
# means higher in PRETERM (the contrast was preterm vs term), so a set with a
# positive NES is up in preterm. fgsea needs the vector NAMED by the gene ID.
rank_outcome <- genes_by_outcome |>
  select(feature, stat) |>
  drop_na(feature, stat) |> # genes DESeq2 could not test have no stat
  arrange(desc(stat)) |>    # fgsea expects a decreasingly ranked vector
  deframe()                 # two columns -> one named vector

# Same identifiers in the ranking and in the sets? Hallmark is built with
# Ensembl IDs here, so the names must line up before anything else matters.
hallmark <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H") |>  # 50 sets
  select(gs_name, ensembl_gene) |>                                  # long format
  filter(!is.na(ensembl_gene))

sets <- split(hallmark$ensembl_gene, hallmark$gs_name)
hallmark_ids <- unique(hallmark$ensembl_gene)
matched_genes <- intersect(names(rank_outcome), hallmark_ids)

# The identifier check, three ways:
# 1. Is every ID in the ranking the same KIND of ID (all Ensembl-shaped)?
all(grepl("^ENSG[0-9]+$", names(rank_outcome)))
# 2. How many ranked genes sit in at least one Hallmark set?
length(matched_genes)
length(matched_genes) / length(rank_outcome)
# 3. How many genes from each set actually match the ranking?
min(vapply(sets, function(ids) sum(ids %in% names(rank_outcome)), integer(1)))

if (anyDuplicated(names(rank_outcome))) {
  stop("The gene ranking contains duplicate feature IDs.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (length(matched_genes) == 0) {
  stop("No ranked Ensembl IDs matched the Hallmark gene sets.", call. = FALSE)
}

# A seed: fgsea shuffles genes at random when it builds its null, so without
# one the padj values move slightly every time you knit.
set.seed(1)
fgsea_outcome <- fgsea(pathways = sets,
                       stats    = rank_outcome,
                       minSize  = 15,
                       maxSize  = 500) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  arrange(padj)

fgsea_outcome |> select(pathway, size, ES, NES, padj, leadingEdge) |> head(10)
```

```{r}
# The two summary numbers the exercise asks for
c(genes_ranked = length(rank_outcome),
  ranked_in_a_set = length(matched_genes),
  sets_tested = nrow(fgsea_outcome),
  sig_padj_05 = sum(fgsea_outcome$padj < 0.05),
  higher_in_preterm = sum(fgsea_outcome$padj < 0.05 &
                            fgsea_outcome$NES > 0),
  higher_in_term = sum(fgsea_outcome$padj < 0.05 &
                            fgsea_outcome$NES < 0))
```
- Sets significant, and how many point each way (26, with 23 higher in preterm)?
